Keywords: Latin marriage banns and children status
RagShortTexts: The 1215 council required public inquiry before marriage; prohibited unions affected children.

Variants.Content: Lateran IV canon51 requires priests to announce an intended marriage so lawful impediments can be raised; doubt pauses the union pending reliable inquiry. It addresses illegitimacy in clandestine unions within prohibited degrees and unions knowingly contracted despite impediments, while punishing malicious false objections. Absence of a grand ceremony does not automatically mean invalidity, and ecclesiastical status is not one uniform land-inheritance law.

A household needs credible witnesses and kin information, not a large feast as proof. An objection can delay work and household formation; a neighbor’s insult is not an adjudication of a child’s status.

Noble alliances also face kinship impediments and proof; publication does not erase a known prohibition. Property claims still require the applicable local inheritance rule rather than an automatic inference from a church label.
